Article Title: Watch: ‘Illegal’ tin shed removed at TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee's Kalighat residence
Article Text:
Footage shows workers dismantling the structure outside Banerjee's Kalighat residence.

NEW DELHI: A temporary tin shed outside TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee 's residence in south Kolkata was removed by the municipal corporation on Wednesday.The incident occoured hours after the Diamond Harbour MP accused Kolkata Police personnel of conducting surveillance around his house and claimed another attack on him was being planned.Footage of the incident shows workers dismantling the structure outside Abhishek's Kalighat residence following police directions. The shed was allegedly erected by encroaching on the footpath.The removal came amid a fresh controversy after Abhishek posted a video on X alleging that police personnel were using official vehicles to conduct reconnaissance near his house and illegally keep him under surveillance.In his post, the Diamond Harbour MP claimed a similar exercise had taken place last week, a day before a group of people allegedly attacked his residence on November 7 during celebrations marking his birthday."Once again, Kolkata Police officials are using vehicles to conduct surveillance around my residence and snoop on me," he said, alleging that police had failed to arrest anyone involved in the incident even after four days."I have serious reasons to believe another attack is being planned," he said, questioning whether the objective was to intimidate him and silence his voice.Alleging misuse of police machinery, Abhishek questioned why the BJP government was afraid of his voice and accused the administration of failing to act despite repeated complaints.Tensions had erupted outside his Kalighat residence on November 7 during celebrations marking his birthday. The TMC MP had alleged a conspiracy to assassinate him and accused the BJP of orchestrating the unrest.Former chief minister Mamata Banerjee had also criticised the BJP over the incident.
Article Summary: A temporary tin shed outside TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee's residence in south Kolkata was removed by the municipal corporation on Wednesday. The shed was allegedly erected by encroaching on the footpath. The incident occoured hours after the Diamond Harbour MP accused police of conducting surveillance around his house and claimed another attack on him was being planned.

Article Title: Arvind Kejriwal, daughter Harshita get death threats from Bishnoi gang; Rs 7 crore demanded
Article Text:
Kejriwal gets death threat in Bishnoi gang's name

NEW DELHI: Former Delhi chief minister and Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal has allegedly received a death threat from a person claiming to be a member of jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi's gang, with the sender demanding Rs 7 crore in extortion, news agency ANI reported.According to a complaint filed by Tilak Nagar MLA Jarnail Singh with the Mohali SSP on November 6, the MLA received threatening phone calls and WhatsApp messages from the alleged gang member.The sender reportedly threatened to kill AAP chief Kejriwal and his daughter, Harshita Kejriwal, if the extortion demand was not met.Mohali Police have registered a case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Information Technology Act. The investigation has been assigned to Inspector Sunil Kumar of the Cyber Crime Police Station.Police are examining the suspect's call records, IP logs and location details as part of the probe.Jarnail Singh has also sought security for Kejriwal and his family, according to the report.
Article Summary: Arvind Kejriwal allegedly receives death threat from person claiming to be member of Lawrence Bishnoi's gang. Sender reportedly demands Rs 7 crore in extortion from former Delhi chief minister. Tilak Nagar MLA Jarnail Singh has filed a complaint with Mohali SSP.

Cong MP in sex abuse row on Manipur poll panels

NEW DELHI: Congress has named Manipur MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, who is facing sexual harassment allegations, as co-chairperson of its manifesto committee and member of its campaign and state poll committees ahead of assembly polls in the state.Akoijam, who represents Inner Manipur in Lok Sabha, has been at the centre of a controversy following complaints by 11 women students at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). He has denied the allegations against him.Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal said Wednesday that party president Mallikarjun Kharge had approved the appointment of additional office bearers for the Manipur Pradesh Congress Committee and the constitution of election committee, campaign committee, manifesto committee, media and publicity committee and election management committee for the ensuing assembly polls in Manipur.Akoijam figures in three committees - co-chairperson in manifesto committee and member in campaign and election committees of the state.After a May 18 complaint by 11 JNU students alleging sexual harassment and misconduct, a five-member committee recommended major disciplinary action. The panel's report went to police on Oct 11, and Vasant Kunj police registered an FIR.Delhi high court stayed his dismissal on Nov 2 and listed his plea for hearing in Jan.

Article Title: Owaisi, Aazad announce alliance for UP polls; send message to Akhilesh
Article Text:
Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad are set to join hands ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, seeking to consolidate Dalit and minority votes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Nagina MP Chandra Shekhar Aazad on Thursday announced their alliance, Samajik Parivartan Morcha, for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with Aazad being the candidate for chief minister.The two leaders made the announcement at a joint press conference in Lucknow, bringing together their parties ahead of the state polls.Azad said the coalition was open to other parties, including the Samajwadi Party and Congress, if they wanted to contest the elections in support of the alliance to prevent the BJP from returning to power in Uttar Pradesh, PTI reported.Rejecting the description of the grouping as a "third front", Azad said it could become a political platform for deprived, oppressed and marginalised sections of society."People have been calling it a third front, but it is not a third front. It is the Samajik Parivartan Morcha. If you understand its depth, you will realise that it is the first front," he said.He said the alliance aimed to bring together weaker and deprived communities and help them use their electoral strength to gain political power and address their concerns.Invoking B R Ambedkar, Azad described political power as the "master key" to resolving people's problems.He argued that communities without their own political organisations could not effectively safeguard their interests, regardless of their population.Azad also cited Ambedkar's formation of political organisations, including the Scheduled Castes Federation, the Indian Labour Party and the Republican Party of India, saying he had recognised that existing political parties would not adequately represent marginalised communities.He further alleged that successive governments had failed to fulfil promises to bring deprived communities into the mainstream, tackle poverty and prevent atrocities against them.While AIMIM has a limited electoral presence in Uttar Pradesh, Owaisi has influence among sections of the minority community. Azad has been seeking to expand his support base among young Dalit voters.Owaisi said that if he and his supporters had to die while fighting for the cause of the people, it would be a worthwhile sacrifice.Taking a swipe at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Owaisi said he would not become the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh and accused him of practising the politics of entitlement.The development comes after Owaisi's attempt to join the INDIA bloc's seat-sharing arrangement in Uttar Pradesh failed to materialise. The AIMIM chief had set an October 2 deadline for the Samajwadi Party and Congress to respond to his proposal, but neither party agreed to include him in the alliance.While AIMIM has a limited electoral presence in Uttar Pradesh, Owaisi has influence among sections of the minority community. Azad, meanwhile, has been seeking to expand his support base among young Dalit voters.
Article Summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Nagina MP Chandra Shekhar Aazad announced their alliance, Samajik Parivartan Morcha, for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Azad is set to be the candidate for chief minister.

Article Title: Babri demolition, 1984 riots, Godhra: Ravi Shankar Prasad takes aim at Sonia Gandhi over memoir
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi holding the memoir

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Senior BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad on Wednesday questioned senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi 's account of her reaction to the Babri Masjid demolition , asking why she had not expressed similar grief over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and the Godhra train burning incident.Reacting to Gandhi's recently released memoir, he alleged that her account lacked honesty and accused her of selective silence on major events during the Congress regime, news agency PTI reported."Every person has the right to write a book on his or her own life. But such a book should have a bit of honesty. That appears to be lacking," Prasad told journalists in his Lok Sabha constituency of Patna Sahib.He questioned why Gandhi had not shed tears when thousands of Sikhs were killed in the 1984 riots in Delhi following Indira Gandhi's assassination. Recalling his role as a lawyer for several riot victims, Prasad also invoked Rajiv Gandhi's controversial remark that "the ground shakes when a big tree falls".Prasad further targeted Gandhi over her criticism of the handling of the 2002 Gujarat riots, asking why she had remained silent over the Godhra train burning incident, in which nearly 60 kar sevaks were killed after coaches of the Sabarmati Express were set on fire.The BJP leader also accused Gandhi of failing to strongly criticise Rajiv Gandhi over the Shah Bano case, in which his government overturned a Supreme Court ruling granting maintenance to a divorced Muslim woman.Her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," was released in India on Tuesday. The 526-page memoir, published by HarperCollins India, traces Sonia Gandhi’s life, from her childhood in post-war Italy and marriage into the Nehru-Gandhi family to the assassination of her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and her eventual entry into politics.
Article Summary: Senior BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad questioned Sonia Gandhi's account of her reaction to the Babri Masjid demolition. He alleged that her account lacked honesty and accused her of selective silence on major events during the Congress regime. Gandhi's memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," was released in India on Tuesday.

Article Title: 20-22 Sunetra Pawar-led NCP MLAs may leave party anytime: Sanjay Raut
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut alleged that NCP legislators had been reduced to "being slaves".

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amid renewed speculation about a merger between the two factions of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Wednesday claimed that 20 to 22 MLAs from the Sunetra Pawar-led faction could break away.Speaking to reporters, Raut said the meetings between NCP legislators and party founder Sharad Pawar were more than casual interactions, suggesting that political realignments could be underway.He also alleged that NCP legislators had been reduced to "being slaves" following the death of Ajit Pawar , PTI reported."20 to 22 MLAs of Sunetra Pawar's party can break away anytime....If they return to their parental home (Sharad Pawar-led NCP), then it is not a merger. Or they may join some other party before the polls," Raut said.Earlier on Tuesday, Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis had said that any merger involving the NCP factions could not take place without consulting the BJP.Responding to the remark, Raut said it did not apply to Sharad Pawar's party.Raut also criticised the Maharashtra government over the controversial election for the chairman's post at Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy, saying the developments were detrimental to democracy.NCP leader Rajesh Patil, a candidate backed by the ruling Mahayuti alliance was elected chairman on Tuesday after the state government nominated four additional directors with voting rights to the dairy's board.Raut alleged that the move helped the ruling alliance overturn the result of last month's board election, in which the panel led by Congress MLC Satej Patil had secured a majority.He accused Mahayuti ministers of stooping to a low level during the episode and warned that "all days are not same in politics".
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut claims that 20 to 22 MLAs from the Sunetra Pawar- led faction could break away. He also alleged that NCP legislators had been reduced to "being slaves" following the death of Ajit Pawar. Raut also criticised the Maharashtra government over the controversial election for the chairman's post.

Article Title: '95% suffer, 5% exploit': Akhilesh says UP polls no longer '80-20' in dig at BJP
Article Text:
Akhilesh Yadav said his 95-5 formula challenges CM Yogi Adityanath's 80-20 narrative (File photo)

Akhilesh announces visits to Ayodhya, Vrindavan

SP chief questions voter list changes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday accused the BJP of creating divisions in Uttar Pradesh and claimed that the state's political contest was now between 95 per cent of people facing hardship and five per cent whom he described as exploiters.His remarks appeared to take a swipe at chief minister Yogi Adityanath's "80-20" formulation, which the BJP leader had popularised ahead of the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections to describe the political divide in the state."The fight is no longer between 80 and 20 per cent. It is now a fight between 95 and five per cent. Ninety-five per cent of the people who are suffering, distressed and humiliated are on one side, while five per cent of exploiters are on the other," Yadav said.He also claimed that the BJP was feeling the pressure of this changing political equation."When there is a fight between 95 and five per cent, BJP leaders will not even know where they have landed. That is why their language and behaviour have changed," Yadav added.Responding to a question about his plans to visit the Ram temple in Ayodhya, the SP chief said he would also visit the Kedareshwar temple in Etawah and Vrindavan."Not just Ayodhya, we will also visit Kedareshwar and Vrindavan," he said.Yadav also gave a new interpretation to the party's PDA slogan, describing it as "First Darshan, Then Blessings".Explaining his remarks, he referred to members of his family and party leaders associated with the names of Hindu deities Shiva and Ram."Both Shiva and Ram are present in our family. We have both -- uncle Shivpal and Ram Gopal Yadav with us."Awadhesh (Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad) and Pawan (Ayodhya assembly candidate Pawan Pandey ) are also with us. So why is the BJP so nervous?" he said.Earlier, Pawan Pandey had announced that Yadav would visit Ayodhya on December 12 to offer prayers to Ram Lalla.The SP president also targeted the government over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, drawing a comparison between a reported drug seizure and claims of large-scale voter deletions."Newspapers reported that cannabis worth Rs 1.27 crore was seized. On the other hand, there is talk of 1.27 crore votes being deleted. What a strange coincidence," he said.Calling for greater transparency in elections, Yadav proposed issuing metal voter identity cards that could not be duplicated or copied. He also suggested linking voter lists with Aadhaar.Turning to infrastructure development, Yadav claimed that the Lucknow, Kanpur and Agra Metro projects were initiated under the previous Samajwadi Party government.He accused the BJP government of failing to expand the metro network significantly in the past decade."Lucknow, Kanpur and Agra Metros were the contribution of the Samajwadi Party government. The BJP government has not been able to extend the metro network even by 10 centimetres in 10 years," he said.Yadav also alleged corruption in the awarding of infrastructure contracts. He claimed that irregularities in the tendering process had affected the quality of roads and expressways, making driving conditions worse and contributing to an increase in accidents.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav says his 95-5 formula challenges Yogi Adityanath's 80-20 narrative. He says the BJP is feeling the pressure of this changing political equation. Yadav also gave a new interpretation to the party's PDA slogan, "First Darshan, Then Blessings"

Article Title: ‘Local DCP suddenly on leave, new DCP in’: CJP's Dipke hints at jail time; Delhi Police detains protesters - top developments
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke, along with Chief Spokesperson Saurav Das, National Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka and Singer Vishal Dadlani during a protest seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter roll deletions at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park.

Journalist Roshie detained: Neha

TMC extends support to CJP

'We follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi': Dipke

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: Diwali crackers cure several diseases, says BJP MLA Papia Adhikari during Kali Puja
Article Text:
BJP’s Tollygunge MLA Papia Adhikari





KOLKATA: Days after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari issued a special message on bursting loud firecrackers during Kali Puja and Diwali celebrations, BJP ’s Tollygunge MLA Papia Adhikari claimed that bursting firecrackers can cure several diseases.Papia Adhikari, the MLA from Tollygunge, had gone to inaugurate a Kali Puja in her constituency.As she began speaking with a microphone in hand, a firecracker went off loudly in front of her. Continuing with her speech, she said, “You will see that bursting firecrackers will cure several diseases.”“Our chief minister has said that we will burst firecrackers. How can Kali Puja be complete without firecrackers? We will definitely burst firecrackers. However, we will follow the guidelines by the police,” she said.Earlier, speaking at the inaugural stages of several Kali Puja pandals, including those at Amherst Street and Khalishani, the CM said that firecrackers will be burst during the festival.However, he urged everyone to ensure that eco-friendly or green crackers are used and that noise pollution regulations are followed.
Article Summary: Papia Adhikari, the MLA from Tollygunge, had gone to inaugurate a Kali Puja in her constituency. As she began speaking with a microphone in hand, a firecracker went off loudly in front of her. “You will see that bursting firecrackers will cure several diseases”

Article Title: Teen killed after rocket hits Mumbai crackers shop, 3 friends run out
Article Text:
16-year-old charred to death after firecracker shop explodes in Mumbai's Malad

Firecracker tragedies

(Inputs by Richa Pinto, V Narayan, Suhas Birhade, BB Nayak, Pradeep Gupta & Nishikant Karlikar)





MUMBAI: Chief fire officer Ravindra Ambulgekar said, "Both Malwani and Pratiksha Nagar blazes were triggered by firecrackers. Each of the calls we attended focused on ensuring that the blaze did not spread. "The city fire brigade attended to 333 fire calls triggered by fireworks between Nov 6 and Nov 10. Of these, police recorded 200 fire accidents due to crackers, a sharp increase from 80 in 2024 and 113 in 2025.In the Malad inferno, residents informed TOI that 16-year-old Shahnawaz Niyaz Khan had entered a firecracker shop with his friends to buy crackers when a rocket allegedly fell on it from outside, triggering a series of explosions. Three of his friends managed to run out but the teen was trapped.The shopkeeper, unaware that he was still inside, rolled down the shutter and fled the site, said Congress MLA Aslam Shaikh.Another mishap struck a row of labourers' hutments in Pratiksha Nagar, Sion, Tuesday. Local BJP corporator Shilpa Keluskar said that six huts caught fire. "Multiple explosions took place as LPG cylinders blasted. One fireman was injured," she said.Negligence took a toll on innocent lives. TV actor Divyanka Tripathi posted a tribute to lift operator Dhanpat Mahto who died in a fatal firecracker blaze in her society, Runwal Elegante in Andheri Lokhandwala, on Nov 6.Saying 'Dhanpat Uncle' wasn't just a guard but part of their everyday lives, she shared a video of him at the gate welcoming her newborn babies. Tripathi said when her boys are older, she will tell them that a kind man had welcomed them.In Vasai-Virar and Mira-Bhayandar, 48 fires were reported Nov 9-10, mostly at garbage dumps. "Most were minor, and our teams doused them quickly. No casualties occurred," said Mira-Bhayandar Municipal Corporation chief fire officer Prakash Borade.Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC) reported 28 fires on Nov 9 and 10, taking the Diwali mishap toll to 90, a disaster management official said.In Ulhasnagar, a major fire broke out at a showroom in Camp 3 on Tuesday, damaging a large showroom.Meanwhile, the deployment of Mumbai fire brigade vehicles to Thane on Nov 8 to assist in firefighting operations at a high-rise society housing deputy CM Eknath Shinde's relatives led to a political controversy.Responding to criticism by opposition leader Kishori Pednekar, Amey Ghole, Shiv Sena (Shinde) group leader in BMC, defended the move, arguing that saving lives during emergencies should take precedence over municipal boundaries.
Article Summary: Mumbai fire brigade attended to 333 fire calls triggered by fireworks between Nov 6 and Nov 10. Of these, police recorded 200 fire accidents due to crackers, a sharp increase from 80 in 2024 and 113 in 2025. In Ulhasnagar, a major fire broke out at a showroom in Camp 3 on Tuesday.

Article Title: 4 govt directors help BJP-led group win Kolhapur's Gokul polls; another form of vote and election chori, says Congress
Article Text:
Maharashtra’s BJP-led Mahayuti alliance secured victory in the Gokul Dairy chief election held recently





KOLHAPUR: Maharashtra ’s governing BJP-led Mahayuti alliance snatched Tuesday a win over Congress-backed group Samavichari Aghadi in a high-stakes election for Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy’s chief, riding on the support of four new govt nominees.Mahayuti candidate, ex-NCP MLA Rajesh Patil, was elected chief after securing 16 votes, three more than his Samavichari rival Patil Chuyekar’s 13.Gokul has a 25-member board of directors, for which elections were held last month. Mahayuti had won 12 posts and Samavichari 13. Neither had the quorum of 14 required for the chief’s election.Mahayuti govt had last week promulgated an ordinance to nominate five members to large cooperatives, four with voting rights.This drew flak from the opposition, which accused govt of attempting to grab Gokul, the state’s largest milk co-operative. Congress LS leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged “adulteration” of the mandate. A Samavichari plea in Bombay HC against the ordinance was rejected Monday.“We have nominated individuals with experience. If one is a gynaecologist, what’s wrong? When the country’s leader of opposition feels the need to intervene in a milk union election, a gynaecologist is just a common citizen,” CM Devendra Fadnavis said on Tuesday.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal denounced the outcome as “another form of vote and election chori”.
Article Summary: BJP-led Mahayuti alliance snatched a win over Congress-backed group Samavichari Aghadi in a high-stakes election for Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy’s chief. Rajesh Patil, ex-NCP MLA, was elected chief after securing 16 votes.

Article Title: 40,000 farmers join protest march over Gokul poll row in Kolhapur
Article Text:
Over 40,000 individuals participated in the 'Sangharsh Morcha' march to protest against the Gokul chairperson election.





KOLHAPUR: Over 40,000 people across Kolhapur district have joined the 'Sangharsh Morcha' march onto the Kolhapur district collectorate over the ongoing row over Gokul chairperson election. Farmers' leader former MP Raju Shetti, Kolhapur MP Shahu Chhatrapati, Sangli MP Vishal Patil, MP Dhairyasheel Mohite - Patil have joined thousands of dairy farmers in the protest march that began from Dasara Chowk.The march has been called after Maharashtra govt promulgated an ordinance to nominate five members to large co-op societies, granting four of them voting rights.This is likely to impact the Gokul chairperson election that is stuck due to lack of quorum. On Monday, people from Kolhapur and adjoining districts of Sangli and Satara also joined the march.
Article Summary: The march has been called after Maharashtra govt promulgated an ordinance to nominate five members to large co-op societies. Farmers' leader former MP Raju Shetti, Kolhapur MP Shahu Chhatrapati, Sangli MP Vishal Patil, MP Dhairyasheel Mohite - Patil have joined thousands of dairy farmers.

Article Title: Cong-backed panel challenges ordinance to appoint govt-nominated members with voting rights to large co-ops in Bombay HC
Article Text:
HC Kolhapur bench

Kolhapur:





The Samavichari Aghadi panel, winning 13 directors’ posts in the Gokul dairy election, on Sunday challenged in Bombay high court’s Kolhapur bench the “constitutional validity” of the ordinance promulgated on Friday allowing state govt to appoint four members to large cooperatives of federal nature with voting rights.Confirming the development, Congress MLC Satej Patil , backing the Samavichari Aghadi, said they had sought directions that the ordinance be scrapped.Three directors elected through the Mahayuti panel have also approached the high court’s Kolhapur bench on Sunday claiming that they had not received notices regarding the petition filed in Kolhapur bench of the Bombay high court regarding a Oct 29 meeting. Both matters would be heard on Monday before the vacation bench of the high court.The election to the chairperson post of Gokul, a Rs 3,000-crore cooperative dairy in Maharashtra, is stuck as Mahayuti alliance won 12 posts and Samavichari Aghadi won 13, both not meeting the quorum required for the election of 14 in the 25-member body. The next meeting to elect the chairperson is scheduled for Nov 10 following interim directions of the Bombay high court.BJP MP Dhananjay Mahadik said, “The meeting on Oct 29 to elect the chairperson was adjourned because of the lack of a quorum.When Samavichari Aghadi moved a petition in the high court against this, the court ordered notices to be issued to 12 directors of Mahayuti regarding the petition. During the hearing on Nov 2, the opposition counsel submitted an affidavit to the court stating that all directors had received the notices. However, in reality, three directors — Ambarishsingh Ghatge, Virendra Mandlik and Karansinha Gaikwad — did not receive any notice. Therefore, they have submitted their own affidavits in the high court and filed a criminal and contempt petition.”Earlier, Maharashtra govt on Friday promulgated an ordinance to amend the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, to appoint five govt-nominated members to the boards of federal cooperative societies with an annual turnover exceeding Rs500 crore and granted four of them voting rights. The move comes amid the ongoing logjam over the election to the chairperson post of Gokul dairy.
Article Summary: The Samavichari Aghadi panel, winning 13 directors’ posts in the Gokul dairy election, on Sunday challenged in Bombay high court’s Kolhapur bench the “constitutional validity” of the ordinance promulgated on Friday. Congress MLC Satej Patil said they had sought directions that the ordinance be scrapped. Both matters would be heard on Monday before the vacation bench of the high court. The election to the chairperson post of the Rs 3,000-crore cooperative dairy is stuck as Mahayuti alliance won 12 posts.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Girl dies in accident, mob thrashes biker
Article Text: Nagpur: An 18-year-old girl on Wednesday died at Sangharsh Nagar Chowk after a speeding biker rammed the scooter on which she was travelling pillion with her mother. An angry mob thrashed the biker and later raised slogans at Govt Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), alleging that prompt treatment could have saved the teenager.As per sources, the biker hit the scooter from behind at high speed. The girl, Aavni Baghel, fell on the road due to the impact and suffered serious head injuries. Her mother and the biker also sustained injuries. Enraged locals caught hold of the biker and assaulted him. The incident created tension at the junction, forcing police personnel to intervene and disperse the crowd.Avani, her mother and the biker were rushed to GMCH, where the girl was declared dead. Her mother’s condition is stated to be out of danger, while the biker is undergoing treatment.Later, a crowd gathered at GMCH alleging delay in providing treatment to Aavni. Nandanvan police were in the process of registering an offence against the biker and launched an investigation.
Article Summary: An 18-year-old girl died after a speeding biker rammed the scooter on which she was travelling pillion with her mother. The girl, Aavni Baghel, fell on the road due to the impact and suffered serious head injuries. Her mother and the biker also sustained injuries.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Cop suspended over woman’s plaint of house trespass, sexual harassment
Article Text:
Cop suspended over woman’s plaint of house trespass, sexual harassment





Tuticorin: A special branch head constable of Tharuvaikulam police station in Tuticorin district has been placed under suspension after a woman accused him of trespassing into her house and making obscene and sexually suggestive gestures while purportedly enquiring about her brother.A case was registered against Selvin Raja, 37, based on a complaint from the victim. The woman alleged that Raja visited her residence on Oct 27 and Nov 2 under the pretext of inquiring about her brother, who was reportedly involved in a matrimonial dispute. On Nov 6, when she was alone at home, the constable entered the premises and behaved in an obscene manner, making sexually suggestive gestures and stating that he had come specifically to see and speak with her, she said.The complainant alleged that when she questioned his repeated visits and raised an alarm, the constable fled. She immediately alerted police and later lodged a formal complaint. Subsequently, DSP M Sundarapandiyan conducted an inquiry with both the complainant and the accused. Based on the findings, police registered a case for house-trespass, sexual harassment and action intended to insult the modesty of a woman under BNS, and Section 4 (harassment of women) of Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.Police said a notice was served on the accused, and departmental action also initiated. Selvin Raja was placed under suspension on Nov 7, and further investigation was underway.
Article Summary: A case was registered against Selvin Raja, 37, based on a complaint from the victim. The woman alleged that Raja visited her residence on Oct 27 and Nov 2 under the pretext of inquiring about her brother. Raja was placed under suspension on Nov 7, and further investigation was underway.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: Court issues notice to BJP’s R Sreelekha in Rahul Gandhi defamation case
Article Text:
R Sreelekha

Kottayam:





A magistrate court in Mavelikkara has issued a notice to BJP state vice-president and former DGP R Sreelekha over an alleged derogatory remark against Leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi The judicial first class magistrate court directed Sreelekha to appear in person in the criminal defamation case based on a complaint filed by KPCC general secretary K P Sreekumar. The case will be taken up again on Dec 2.The complaint relates to Sreelekha’s alleged remarks during a BJP Janasabha programme at Punalur on Oct 14. She allegedly said that what Gandhi displayed in Delhi was agitation and frenzy caused by excessive intake of drugs.According to the complainant, he sent Sreelekha a legal notice through his lawyer seeking an apology and compensation, but received no response. The court issued its order after considering the statements of three witnesses and evidence, including video footage, he said.Sreekumar said he would continue legal proceedings until she tendered an apology. The court’s notice was a setback to the former DGP’s “arrogance” in believing she could say anything, he added.Separately, Punalur police had earlier registered a case against Sreelekha, including a charge of incitement to riot, on a complaint filed by Youth Congress with the state police chief.
Article Summary: A magistrate court in Mavelikkara has issued a notice to BJP state vice- president and former DGP R Sreelekha over an alleged derogatory remark against Rahul Gandhi. She allegedly said that what Gandhi displayed in Delhi was agitation and frenzy caused by excessive intake of drugs.

Article Title: HC questions varsity’s demand for apology from suspended students
Article Text:
Kerala High Court adjourned the petition to next Friday to enable the university to take a decision on the matter. If the university sticks to its decision, the matter can be heard on merits, the court said.

Kochi:





Kerala High Court on Wednesday criticised Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady, for its demand that the 16 suspended students apologise for allegedly staging a mock cremation of vice-chancellor Ciza Thomas during a protest.Justice P V Kunhikrishnan said the students had already been under suspension for more than 60 days and asked what more the university expected them to endure. He was considering a petition filed by Archana P S of Palakkad and other students challenging their suspension and seeking permission to appear for the examinations.“They are students. Which politicians or leaders have not engaged in such activities as protests during their student days? The court has never supported, accepted or justified such protests. But they have suffered for 60 days and were not allowed to write the examination. Why don’t you interfere in the matter? What do they have to do to write the exam?” the court asked the university’s senior counsel. It also observed that the students and their parents would be the ultimate sufferers, whatever be the outcome.The court questioned the maintainability of two FIRs registered against the students over the protest.The state clarified that one FIR concerned an alleged attack on a police officer, while the other was registered on a complaint lodged by the vice-chancellor.HC adjourned the petition to next Friday to enable the university to take a decision on the matter. If the university sticks to its decision, the matter can be heard on merits, the court said.Earlier, the single bench had passed an interim order provisionally permitting the petitioners to appear for the examination. However, a division bench later set it aside. Supreme Court, on an appeal, remanded the case to the single bench and directed it to decide the matter afresh after hearing the parties expeditiously.
Article Summary: HC adjourned the petition to next Friday to enable the university to take a decision on the matter. If the university sticks to its decision, the matter can be heard on merits, the court said. Supreme Court, on an appeal, remanded the case to the single bench and directed it to decide the matter afresh.

Article Title: Woman found hanging in Godda home, father alleges murder over Maiya Samman money
Article Text:
Priyanka‘s body was found hanging from a ceiling fan with a dupatta. Her father Bittu Sao accused Sunil and his mother of killing Priyanka and making it appear a suicide

Dumka:





A 28-year-old woman was found hanging from a ceiling fan in her home in Mohani village under Mahagama police station limits of Godda district on Wednesday. The deceased was identified as Priyanka Kumari , the wife of Sunil Sao. Priyanka’s parents claimed she was murdered over a dispute linked to the monthly stipend under state govt’s Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana (MMSY). The couple have three children.Priyanka‘s body was found hanging from a ceiling fan with a dupatta. Her father Bittu Sao accused Sunil and his mother of killing Priyanka and making it appear a suicide. Bittu claimed money recieved by Priyanka under the scheme had strained the couple’s relationship. “Sunil had purchased a mobile phone with the money my daughter received under MMSY. This had triggered arguments between them. They frequently fought over the money,” Bittu claimed.He further said the coupled had an argument earlier on Wednesday and claimed Priyanka was assaulted before being killed and her body was hung from the ceiling fan. Bittu also alleged that Sunil wanted to marry another woman, which further strained the marriage.Sunil informed the police that he was harvesting paddy in the evening when Priyanka committed suicide. Abhinav Anand, the officer in-charge of Mahagama police station, said, “Prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicide. However, all aspects of the incident are being examined. The deceased’s family have not submitted a written complaint so far. Priyanka’s body has been sent to the hospital for postmortem examination. ”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Priyanka Kumari, the wife of Sunil Sao. Her parents claimed she was murdered over a dispute linked to the monthly stipend under state govt’s Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana (MMSY)

Article Title: Man arrested for attempting to murder his neighbour in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Ukkadam police in the city arrested a man on charges attempting to murder his neighbour by attacking him with an iron rod following a dispute between them near Kottaimedu on Wednesday.The arrested man has been identified as V Sivaraman, 58, of Vincent Road in Kottaimedu.According to police, a dispute broke out between Sivaraman and his neighbour, C Prabhu, 42, on Monday.On Wednesday, when Prabhu was standing in front of Sivaraman’s house, Sivaraman picked a quarrel with him, abused him and threatened him with dire consequences. Further, in the heat of the moment, Sivaraman attacked Prabhu on the head and hands with an iron rod, leaving him injured.Prabhu’s wife, Sathiya, rushed him to Coimbatore Medical College Hospital in a 108 ambulance and later lodged a complaint with the Ukkadam police. Police registered a case under sections 296(b) and 109 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Sivaraman was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested man has been identified as V Sivaraman, 58, of Vincent Road in Kottaimedu. Police registered a case under sections 296(b) and 109 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. He was remanded in judicial custody.
